title: A replay of real work can cross the wait chunk on a slow host, and the documents only say how to shorten it
foundBy: session agent, maintainer of this repository, after repeated replays of one recorded campaign on a shared host
details:
**What this is.** SAC-033 asks for `--record` and `--replay`, and lists what a replay has to hold still. A cassette fixes what the models say. It cannot fix how long an agent's real work takes, such as a package install. So the question is which timers in this harness turn elapsed time into control flow.

**The wait chunk does.** `wait` returns when its chunk elapses, 240 seconds by default, whether or not a reply arrived, and it tells the model to call `wait` again. A live orchestrator does. A recorded orchestrator does whatever it did when recorded. Suppose a dispatch took under 240 seconds in the recording and takes longer in the replay. The proxy tolerates the changed tool result, and the recorded orchestrator then reads and accepts a reply that does not exist yet. The conversation replays with no miss, and the delivery is wrong. The other direction is harmless, and it was observed. A chunk that elapsed in the recording returned a judgment in the replay, the next recorded `wait` returned at once, and the delivery was identical.

**The setting already exists.** `CS_CAMPAIGN_WAIT_SECONDS` overrides the chunk, `--for` included, and `create` forwards it to the members. The function `WaitChunk` accepts any value, so it can go above the default as well as below it. SPEC §6.1 and R126, and the manual, present it only as the way a replay tier shortens a wait. A replay of real work needs the opposite. The ceiling is the tool call timeout that the recorded model asked for, which is part of the recording and so is constant. In the recording studied it was 900 seconds, so a chunk of 840 seconds is safe and gives three and a half times the default.

**What is asked for.** Say in the manual and in SPEC §6.1 that a replay whose agents do real work should raise the chunk. Say what bounds it, and add the doc claim test that keeps the sentence true. Consider making an elapsed chunk visible outside the model, so that a wrapper can fail a replay whose `wait` elapsed where the recorded one returned a judgment. Today only the model is shown that line.

**How to reproduce.** Replay a recorded campaign on a host slow enough that one dispatch takes more than 240 seconds where the recording took less. The replay ends with no miss and a wrong delivery. Set `CS_CAMPAIGN_WAIT_SECONDS=840` and it passes.

notes.text: Corrected on the day it was filed, after reading the source. The first text named three timers, and two of the claims were wrong. The stall threshold does not fire on slow work. Each turn driver calls a stall only when the agent is no longer working. The opencode driver asks the server whether the session is busy. The claude and codex drivers check the TUI state as well as the transcript. A long silent tool call is busy. The readback bound of 15 minutes is about fifteen times a healthy readback, so it is not a practical risk either. The type went from defect to improvement and the severity from med to low, because the setting that solves the remaining case already exists and is forwarded.
